items.b: GOLD $4,307.50 AND PLATINUM $1,713.00: EVERY MARK LOWER SINCE FRIDAY 28 AUGUST
items.t: Both metals have printed a lower reading on this tape at every mark since 28 August. Gold has given up $297.00 or 6.45% across five marks, platinum $170.00 or 9.03%. All four metals were re-read at press time and all four written back to the tape.

items.b: SILVER HAS LOST MORE THAN ANY OF THEM, AND GOLD THE LEAST
items.t: Since 28 August silver is down 9.68% to $63.56, platinum 9.03%, palladium 6.88% to $1,286.00 and gold 6.45%. The gold-silver ratio is 67.77 against 65.43. That is the order a board takes when the trade sells the whole complex rather than one metal.

items.b: THE ONE-CARAT LAB-GROWN REFERENCE FALLS A THIRD TIME, TO $675
items.t: CaratRadar's one-carat average is $675, down $12 on the day and $25 from Monday's $700, a fall of 3.57% across three readings. The same page's whole-market index rose $12 to $1,535 over the same day, and active listings gained 7,128 to 1,211,846.

items.b: A £5,000 ESTIMATE MEETS A £59,000 BID: STEEL PATEK FROM A CORNISH JEWELLERY BOX
items.t: A stainless Calatrava reference 448, found during a house clearance in Camborne, sold at Hansons Cornwall in Penzance on 25 August for 11.8 times its low estimate and 5.9 times its high. The buyer bid by telephone from Hong Kong.

items.b: KERING PUTS NEW CHIEFS INTO POMELLATO AND DODO AND SENDS SABINA BELLI TO KERING ITALIA
items.t: Charlotte Fournet takes Pomellato and Krizia Cucurachi takes DoDo from 15 September, both reporting to Jean-Marc Duplaix. The division took 521 million euros in the first half, up 14%, inside a group whose revenue fell 3% to 7.22 billion euros.

items.b: $24,900 FOR A RUBBER BIG BANG, AND 1,600 SQUARE FEET AT SOUTH COAST PLAZA
items.t: Hublot's Big Bang Original Soft Touch launched 1 September with texture overmoulded into case, bezel, dial and strap rather than coated on. Jessica McCormack opened its second US store on 28 August, with Rodeo Drive announced for 2027.

tape_ts: 2 Sep 2026 - Kitco, re-read by the Editor at press time and written back to the tape under the One-Price Rule. A metals story leads, so all four were re-read off the board (its own timestamp 05:58 EST) and all four had moved off the 05:00 mark: gold $4,307.50 (down $20.20, 0.4668%), silver $63.56 (down $0.394, 0.6161%), platinum $1,713.00 (down $24.00, 1.3817%) and palladium $1,286.00 (down $1.00, 0.0777%), each against the prior close the 05:00 file already carried, so value, prev and change stay one self-consistent series. Second page for gold: Trading Economics spot $4,305.69, 0.065% off Kitco's $4,308.50 midpoint, inside the agreement band, so no outside-source divergence is disclosed this session. CNBC's quote pages returned HTTP 403 to this desk this morning and Trading Economics was named and used in their place. The lab-grown one-carat reference was re-verified independently at press time on CaratRadar's own page text and was unchanged at $675, so it was not written back. NAT1 and LGD1 on the chips below are rendered from prices.json and lab-prices.json by the build and are not this tape's marks.
